summary:
Format and return a string. The full format specification is %[flag][width][.precision]type.

The supported conversion controls are listed below. Flags may be combined.

Flags

" " - For integers and floating-point values, prefix a positive value with a space and a negative value with a minus sign.
"+" - Always output the sign of an integer or floating-point value. Without this flag, only negative values have a sign.
"-" - Left-align the field. Otherwise use the default, which is right alignment.
"|" - Center the field.
"=" - Use column mode for strings longer than the field width, wrapping them onto multiple lines.
"#" - Use table mode for strings, placing lists of words within the field on lines separated by '\n'.
"0" - Place this immediately before the width integer to pad empty positions with 0 until the field reaches its specified width.
"'X'" - Pad the field with the character inside the single quotes, rather than the default space. If both zero padding and character padding are specified, the later setting takes precedence. To pad with an apostrophe, double quote, or backslash, use the escapes `\'`, `\"`, `\\`.
"@" - The argument is an array. Apply all format information other than "@" to every array element.

Minimum output width

An integer sets the minimum field width. Use '*' to take the width from the output argument list. If the actual output is wider, use its actual width; if it is shorter, pad with spaces or zeros.

Precision (.precision)

".整数" (integer precision) - Set field precision. Ordinary strings are truncated beyond this length. If precision exceeds the field width, the width becomes the precision. In table mode, precision specifies the number of columns; if omitted, the best fit is calculated automatically.
":整数" (width and precision) - Set both width and precision. A leading 0 pads the field with zeros instead of spaces.

Types

% - Output a percent sign, for example printf("%%");
O - Format an LPC value of any type, useful for debugging.
s - Format a string.
d, i - Output an integer as a signed decimal value; i is the older form.
c - Output an integer as a character.
o - Output an integer as an unsigned octal value without a 0 prefix.
x - Output an integer as unsigned hexadecimal without a 0x prefix, using lowercase a-f.
X - Output an integer as unsigned hexadecimal without a 0x prefix, using uppercase A-F.
f - Format a floating-point value.
